"Moonlight" cinematographer James Laxton used lyrical, introspective style with muted blues/greens/yellows, 1.85:1 aspect ratio, close-ups, and available light
"The Florida Project" cinematographer Alexis Zabe used vibrant, playful style with bright pastels/neons, 2.39:1 aspect ratio, handheld and Steadicam work, and natural light
Laxton used natural light extensively in "Moonlight", shooting during golden hour or overcast days, augmenting with practical sources like lamps and candles, avoiding harsh artificial light
Zabe used natural light extensively in "The Florida Project", shooting during golden hour, adding neon signs and string lights for color, with bold saturated colors for fantasy
"Joker" cinematographer Lawrence Sher used a mix of 35mm and IMAX formats, with handheld camera work and natural lighting for realism; IMAX scenes added grandeur
assistant|filmmaking_training: "Clemency" cinematographer Eric Branco used a muted color palette, static camera shots, close-ups, and natural lighting to convey bleakness and claustrophobia
"The Miseducation of Cameron Post" cinematographer Ashley Connor used a warm muted palette, handheld camera work, soft focus, and natural lighting to create nostalgia and intimacy
"Clemency" composer Kathryn Bostic and sound designers Damian Volpe and Ren Klyce used a minimalist score, diegetic prison sounds, silence, and recurring fragmented piano motifs
"The Miseducation of Cameron Post" composer Julian Wass and sound designers Jordan Pereira and Kent Sparling used indie-folk influences, diegetic music, soundscapes, and quiet moments
"Clemency" casting director Avy Kaufman worked with director Chinonye Chukwu to cast the film
